import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_29/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_29/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# According to operation_history: JOIN : [["Source2_29_0", "Source2_29_1"], ["movie id", "movie_id"]]
# Join df0 and df1 on df0["movie id"] == df1["movie_id"]

# Perform inner join to keep only matching movie ids
joined_df = pd.merge(df0, df1, left_on="movie id", right_on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Target schema: ['movie title': string, 'movie id': integer, 'user_id': integer, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': integer]
# The joined_df columns after merge: ['movie id', 'movie title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating']

# Ensure correct column order and types
result_df = joined_df[['movie title', 'movie id', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating']].copy()

# Enforce data types as per target schema
result_df['movie title'] = result_df['movie title'].astype(str)
result_df['movie id'] = result_df['movie id'].astype(int)
result_df['user_id'] = result_df['user_id'].astype(int)
result_df['movie_id'] = result_df['movie_id'].astype(int)
result_df['rating'] = result_df['rating'].astype(int)

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_29/target_multisource.csv"
result_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_29/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_29/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source2_29_0 and Source2_29_1 on movie id = movie_id
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, left_on="movie id", right_on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Group by 'movie title' (the primary key) and aggregate other columns with MIN to ensure uniqueness and match target keys
result = joined.groupby("movie title", as_index=False).agg({
    "movie id": "min",
    "user_id": "min",
    "movie_id": "min",
    "rating": "min"
})

# Write the final output with exact target schema and column order
result = result[["movie title", "movie id", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating"]]

result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_29/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
